units.la: Huiusmodi sacrificia spiritualia obtinent in ecclesia nostra, tanquam â Deo præcepta & mandata. Reliqua ab hominibus inventa, tradita humanitûs, nec observamus nec moramur, quia frustra Deum colunt, qui docent mandata hominum, Matth. 15: 9.
units.tr: Sacrifices of this spiritual kind hold good in our Church, as commanded and enjoined by God. The rest, invented by men and handed down by human authority, we neither observe nor value, because in vain do they worship God who teach the commandments of men, Matt. 15:9.

units.la: Tertius articulus, in quo concordant universi sectarij, quod pleriq; omnes sectarum duces quaedam confingunt de catholicis doctoribus mendacia, quæ persuadeant imperito populo esse doctrinam papisticam.
units.tr: The third article, in which all the sects agree: that most of the leaders of the sects invent certain lies about the Catholic teachers, which they persuade the untaught people are the doctrine of the Papists.

units.la: Revera phreneticis similes sunt scriptores papistici. Sicut enim illi dum turpissima quæque agunt aut dicunt, non saltem pudoris nihil habent, sed sibi videntur magnifica dixisse & fecisse: Ita hi dum mendacia pro libitu dicunt & scribunt, non saltem pudorem non habent, sed sibi præterea applaudunt, & aliis quod ipsi faciunt impudenter attribuunt. Scribit Harscher sectariorum ducibus commune esse quaedam quadam confingere de catholicis Doctoribus mendacia, quae persuadeant imperito populo esse doctrinam papisticam. Si mendacia scribere nota est Ducum sectariorum, Jesuita Harscher in exercitu sectariorum erit Generalis. Qui plaustra mendaciorum de nostris ecclesiis scripsit in secularibus hisce parallelis, quae imperito populo persuadere vult esse nostram doctrinam, quae non est. Sed relinquo haec.
units.tr: Truly the Papist writers are like madmen. For just as they, while doing or saying the most shameful things, not only have no shame but think they have said and done glorious things, so these, while saying and writing lies at will, not only have no shame but also applaud themselves and shamelessly attribute to others what they themselves do. Harscher writes that it is common for the leaders of the sects to invent certain lies about the Catholic teachers, which they persuade the untaught people are the doctrine of the Papists. If writing lies is characteristic of the leaders of the sects, then the Jesuit Harscher will be the General in the army of the sects, he who in these secular parallels has written a cartload of lies about our churches, which he wishes to persuade the untaught people is our doctrine, though it is not. But I leave these things.

units.la: I. Calvinus scribit catholicos ἀρτολάτρας, hoc est, panicolas: cum optime noverit dogma verum & catholicum, panem in eucharistia non adesse, Christum praesentem adorari.
units.tr: I. Calvin writes that the Catholics are artolatrae, that is, bread-worshippers, although he knew well the true and Catholic dogma, that bread is not present in the Eucharist and that Christ is adored as present.

units.la: Transsubstantiatione esse dogma ecclesiae Pontificiae novit Calvinus, esse vero dogma verum & catholicum ipse non credidit, sensit potius esse dogma falsum, novum scripturae sacrae contrarium, contra fidem apostolicam & naturam Christi. Unde concludebat; si
units.tr: Calvin knew that transubstantiation is a dogma of the Papal Church, but he did not himself believe it to be a true dogma; he rather judged it a false dogma, new and contrary to Holy Scripture, against the apostolic faith and the nature of Christ. Hence he concluded: if

units.la: in eucharistia panis non mutatur in corpus Christi, sed mutatio tantum est sacramentalis manente substantia panis: sequitur Pontificios esse ἀρτολάτρας hoc est, panis adoratores. Nam si antecedens verum est, consequens quoque verum esse necesse est. Et per consequens nullum mendacium dixit Calvinus.
units.tr: in the Eucharist the bread is not changed into the body of Christ, but the change is only sacramental, the substance of the bread remaining, it follows that the Papists are artolatrae, that is, bread-worshippers. For if the antecedent is true, the consequent must also be true. And consequently Calvin told no lie.

units.la: Sed de antecedente quaeritur. Fundamentum sententiae Calvinianae est triplex, quia Transsubstantiatio qua pontificii fingunt panem mutari in corpus Christi. 1. ex scriptura sacra probari non poterit. Sic docet Cajetanus Cardinalis, Occamus, Gabriel Biel, Scotus. Atque hic postremus cum se implicatum videret, aliud principium quaesivit, ecclesiae nimirum Romanae authoritatem, cum ait: Dicendum quod ecclesia declaravit ipsum intellectum (panem converti in corpus Christi & vinum in sanguinem eius) esse de veritate fidei in symbolo symbolo edito sub Innocentio III. in Concilio Lateranensi lib. IV. dist. II. q. 3.
units.tr: But the antecedent is in question. The foundation of the Calvinist view is threefold, because transubstantiation, by which the Papists feign that bread is changed into the body of Christ, 1. cannot be proved from Holy Scripture. So teach Cajetan the Cardinal, Ockham, Gabriel Biel, and Scotus. And the last of these, seeing himself entangled, sought another principle, namely the authority of the Roman Church, when he says: It must be said that the Church has declared that this very meaning (that bread is converted into the body of Christ and wine into his blood) belongs to the truth of faith in the creed issued under Innocent III at the Fourth Lateran Council, book IV, distinction II, question 3.

units.la: II. Quia tempore primitivæ eccle- siæ hoc dogma ignotum fuit. Hoc quatuor argumentis probari potest.
units.tr: II. Because in the time of the primitive Church this dogma was unknown. This can be proved by four arguments.

units.la: I. Ex locutionibus & phrasibus, quibus illi in hoc mysterio explicando usi sunt. Nam panem & vinum in eucharistia appellarunt typos, figuras, imagines, symbola & signa corporis Christi, quæ locutiones transsubstantiationi sunt contrariæ. Tertullianus: hoc est corpus meum dicendo, id est figura corporis mei. Nazianzenus: mensam Domini, id est, panem & vinum, τὰς τύπους τῆς ἡμῶν σωτηρίας, typos nostræ salutis esse. Chrysostomus: iflam mensam præparavit, servis & ancillis in conspectu eorum quotidie, in similitudinem corporis & sanguinis Christi. Augustinus: Non dubitavit Dominus dicere, hoc est corpus meum, cum signum daret corporis sui. adverf. Adimant. Manich. cap. 12.
units.tr: I. From the expressions and phrases which they used in explaining this mystery. For they called the bread and wine in the Eucharist types, figures, images, symbols and signs of the body of Christ, and such expressions are contrary to transubstantiation. Tertullian: by saying "This is my body," he meant the figure of my body. Nazianzen: the table of the Lord, that is, the bread and wine, are the types [τὰς τύπους τῆς ἡμῶν σωτηρίας] of our salvation. Chrysostom: he prepared this table for his servants and handmaids before their eyes every day, in the likeness of the body and blood of Christ. Augustine: The Lord did not hesitate to say, "This is my body," when he gave the sign of his body. Against Adimantus the Manichaean, chap. 12.

units.la: I
units.tr: I

units.la: 2. Quia perspicuè docuerunt sensum literalem hic non esse attendendum, sed verba Christi spiritualiter esse intelligenda. Sic Origenes: Si secundum literam sequaris hoc quod dictum est, nisi manducaveritis carnem filij hominis & biberitis sanguinem meum, hæc litera occidit. Tertullianus: Paulo ante carnem suam panem quoq; cœlestem pronuntiaverat, urgens usq; quaq; per allegoriam necessariorum memoriam Patrum.
units.tr: 2. Because they clearly taught that the literal sense is not to be regarded here, but that the words of Christ must be understood spiritually. Thus Origen: If you follow according to the letter what has been said, "Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink my blood," this letter kills. Tertullian: A little before, he had also called his flesh the heavenly bread, urging at every point, by allegory, the memory of the necessary things of the Fathers.

units.la: Augustinus multis in locis sensum spiritualem urget. Et ex hoc Patre Glossator ad distin. 2. de consec. hæc notat verba: Cœleste Sacramentum quod verè carnem repræsentat, corpus Christi dicitur suo modo, non in rei veritate sed significante mysterio, ut sensus sit, vocatur corpus Christi, id est significat.
units.tr: Augustine often insists on the spiritual sense. And from this Father the Glossator, on distinction 2 of De consecratione, notes these words: The heavenly Sacrament, which truly represents the flesh, is called the body of Christ in its own way, not in the reality of the thing but in a signifying mystery, so that the sense is: it is called the body of Christ, that is, it signifies.

units.la: 3. Quia docuerunt carnem & sanguinem Christi, non corporaliter sed spiritualiter sumenda esse. Augustinus: quid paras dentem & ventrem, crede & manducasti. Cyprianus: Non dentes ad mordendum acuimus, sed fide sincera panem sanctum frangimus & partimur, dum quod divinum & humanum est distinguimus & separamus. Augustinus in Psal. 98. Christum introducit sic seipsum explicantem; non hoc corpus, quod videtis manducaturi estis, & bibituri istum sanguinem, quem fusuri sunt, qui me crucifigent, sacramentum aliquod vobis commendavi spiritualiter intellectum vivificabit vos.
units.tr: 3. Because they taught that the flesh and blood of Christ are to be received not bodily but spiritually. Augustine: Why do you prepare teeth and belly? Believe, and you have eaten. Cyprian: We do not sharpen our teeth for biting, but with sincere faith we break and share the holy bread, while we distinguish and separate what is divine and what is human. Augustine on Psalm 98 introduces Christ explaining himself thus: Not this body which you see you are going to eat, nor the blood which they who crucify me are going to shed you are going to drink; I have commended to you some sacrament, understood spiritually, which will give you life.

units.la: 4. Quia quotiescunque de corpore Christi locuti sunt, ubique illud visibile, palpabile & circumscriptum esse docuerunt. Sic Ignatius, Augustinus, Fulgentius, Theodoretus, alii. E contra Transsubstantiatores, invisibile, impalpabile, incircumscriptum.
units.tr: 4. Because whenever they spoke of the body of Christ, they taught everywhere that it is visible, palpable and circumscribed. Thus Ignatius, Augustine, Fulgentius, Theodoret, and others. On the contrary, the transubstantiationists hold it invisible, impalpable and uncircumscribed.

units.la: Fatendum Patres multis in locis panem corpus Christi, & vinum sanguinem eius appellasse, ad maiorem reverentiam excitandam. Quomodo revera panis in eucharistia non amplius est panis communis sed significativus corpus Christi & vinum non amplius est vinum scilicet commune sed sacrū signum repræsentans sanguinem Christi. Quô respectu si quis panem eucharisticum appellat corpus Christi & vinum sanguinem Christi non errat, quia harum rerum per consecrationem mutatio facta est non realis sed sacramentalis; ita ut si quis effunderet ex malitia vinum eucharisticum, morte omninô afficiendus esset, quia reputaretur ac si ipsum sanguinem Christi effudisset.
units.tr: It must be admitted that the Fathers in many places called the bread the body of Christ, and the wine his blood, in order to stir up greater reverence. In this way, indeed, the bread in the Eucharist is no longer common bread but is significative of the body of Christ, and the wine is no longer common wine but a holy sign representing the blood of Christ. In this respect, if anyone calls the Eucharistic bread the body of Christ and the wine the blood of Christ, he is not wrong, because the change of these things brought about by consecration is not real but sacramental; so that if anyone wickedly poured out the Eucharistic wine, he would deserve to be punished with death, because he would be considered as if he had poured out the very blood of Christ.

units.la: III. Quia evertit articulos fidei, nativitatem Christi ex B. virgine, ascensionem in cœlum, sessionem ad dextram Dei Patris. Nam Christus quatenus à sacerdote creatur non est genitus ex Maria, imò non offertur Mariæ filius, sed sacerdotis creatura; quatenus offertur ut hostia, non est in statu exaltationis: destruit etiam naturam humanam Christi, quod ex collatione doctrinæ pontificiæ & naturæ humanæ Christi facilè intelligi potest.
units.tr: III. Because it overturns the articles of faith: the birth of Christ from the blessed Virgin, his ascension into heaven, his sitting at the right hand of God the Father. For Christ, insofar as he is created by the priest, was not begotten of Mary; indeed, he is not offered as the son of Mary but as the creature of the priest; insofar as he is offered as a victim, he is not in the state of exaltation. It also destroys the human nature of Christ, which can easily be understood from a comparison of the Papist doctrine with the human nature of Christ.

units.la: Et quia dato uno absurdo, alia sequuntur infinita, hinc tot ἀτοπήματα, & doctrinæ quæ maxima cum ignominia & contumelia gloriosissimi servatoris nostri, coniunctæ sunt, obtinent in ecclesia Romana. Utpote 1. Transsubstantiatio dicitur etiam cum substantia non mutatur in substantiâ.
units.tr: And because, once one absurdity is granted, infinitely many others follow, hence so many absurdities [ἀτοπήματα] and doctrines, joined with the greatest disgrace and insult to our most glorious Saviour, prevail in the Roman Church. Namely: 1. Transubstantiation is said to take place even when the substance is not changed into another substance.

units.la: 2. Corpus non est circumscriptum.
units.tr: 2. The body is not circumscribed.

units.la: 3. Datur humanum corpus absq; forma corporis.
units.tr: 3. A human body is given without the form of a body.

units.la: 4. Datur corpus quantum absq; quantitate, longum absq; longitudine, visibile absq; visibilitate.
units.tr: 4. A body is given that is extended without extension, long without length, visible without visibility.

units.la: 5. Christus habet duo corpora, genitum & creatum.
units.tr: 5. Christ has two bodies, one begotten and one created.

units.la: 6. Accidentia sunt accidentia etiamsi nulli accidant.
units.tr: 6. Accidents are accidents even when they inhere in nothing.

units.la: 7. Sacratissimum corpus Christi à moribus editur.
units.tr: 7. The most holy body of Christ is eaten by mice.

units.la: 8. Panis potest fieri DEVS.
units.tr: 8. Bread can become God.

units.la: 9. Creatura potest creare suum creatorem.
units.tr: 9. A creature can create its own Creator.

units.la: 10. Accidens inseparabile potest separari.
units.tr: 10. An inseparable accident can be separated.

units.la: 11. Per benedictionem divinam res creata destruitur.
units.tr: 11. Through the divine blessing a created thing is destroyed.

units.la: 12. Datur axioma non identicum, licet praedicatum idem sit cum subjecto.
units.tr: 12. There is given an axiom that is not an identity, although the predicate is the same as the subject.

units.la: 13. Axioma verum esse potest, etiam cum praedicatum falsò enuntiatur de subjecto.
units.tr: 13. An axiom can be true even when the predicate is falsely asserted of the subject.

units.la: Item illa quae leguntur in missali Romano, de defectibus circa missam occurrentibus, cap. 10.
units.tr: Likewise those things which are read in the Roman Missal, concerning the defects that occur around the Mass, chap. 10.

units.la: 14. Si sacerdos evomat eucharistiam, si species integrae appareant, reverenter sumantur, nisi nausea adsit. Eheu sanctissimum & gloriosissimum corpus Christi in puditissimo vomitu ebriosi sacerdotis iacebit? Ubi est pudor istorum hominum?
units.tr: 14. If the priest vomits the Eucharist, and the species appear intact, let them be reverently taken, unless nausea is present. Alas, will the most holy and glorious body of Christ lie in the most shameful vomit of a drunken priest? Where is the shame of these men?

units.la: 15. Si post consecrationem cecideri musca, aut aliquid ejusmodi & fiat nausea sacerdoti, extrahat eam & lavet cum vino, finita missa comburat (nempe quia bibit sanguinem Christi) & combustio ac lotio hujusmodi in sacrarium projiciatur, si autem non fuerit nausea ei nec ullum periculum timeat, sumat (muscam) cum sanguine.
units.tr: 15. If after the consecration a fly or something of that kind falls in, and the priest feels nausea, let him extract it and wash it with wine; after the Mass is finished let him burn it (namely because it has drunk the blood of Christ), and the ashes and washings of this kind are to be cast into the sacrarium; but if there is no nausea and he fears no danger, let him take (the fly) with the blood.

units.la: 16. Si in hyeme sanguis congeletur in calice, involvatur calix pannis calefactis, si non proficeret ponatur in ferventi aqua prope altare, donec liquescat.
units.tr: 16. If in winter the blood congeals in the chalice, let the chalice be wrapped in warm cloths; if this does not help, let it be placed in hot water near the altar until it melts.

units.la: Talis exstitit Theologia Pontificia à seculo duodecimo, quando Innocentius in Concilio Lateranensi transsubstantiationem decimum tertium articulum symboli Apostolici esse voluit.
units.tr: Such was the Papist theology from the twelfth century, when Innocent, in the Lateran Council, wished transubstantiation to be the thirteenth article of the Apostles' Creed.

units.la: Pergit. Calvinus dicit cultum imaginum esse idololatriam, cùm probè noverit, imagines non aliter coli à catholicis, nisi ut signa amicorum Dei, nullo modo ut Deus, aut idola haberi.
units.tr: He goes on: Calvin says that the worship of images is idolatry, although he knows well that images are not venerated by Catholics otherwise than as signs of the friends of God, and in no way are they regarded as God or as idols.

units.la: Pontificii non negant se adorare imagines, sed negant quod adorando imagines sint idololatrae. Harscherus huius negationis argumentum profert, quia imagines non aliter coluntur à catholicis, nisi ut signa amicorum Dei, nullo modo ut Deus aut idola haberi.
units.tr: The Papists do not deny that they adore images, but they deny that by adoring images they become idolaters. Harscher brings forward the argument for this denial: because images are not venerated by Catholics otherwise than as signs of the friends of God, in no way as God or as idols.

units.la: Ego huic argumento insistam, nec diffusè agam de iis, quae circa hanc materiam dici possent. Dico igitur Calvinum non mentiri, cùm scribit pontificios adorando imagines esse idololatras.
units.tr: I will insist on this argument, nor will I treat at length the things that could be said about this matter. I say, therefore, that Calvin does not lie when he writes that the Papists, by adoring images, are idolaters.

units.la: Primò, quia ut dixi fatentur se adorare imagines, quod sufficit ad asserendam idololatriam, cum imagines naturâ non sint Dij, Gal. 4; 8.
units.tr: First, because, as I said, they confess that they adore images, which is enough to establish idolatry, since images by nature are not gods, Gal. 4:8.

units.la: Secundò, quia adorant crucem, ex quavis materia fabricatam cum hac precatiuncula:
units.tr: Second, because they adore the cross, made of any material, with this little prayer:

units.la: O Crux ave spes unica Auge piis justitiam Regisq; dona veniam.
units.tr: O Cross, hail, our only hope, increase justice in the pious and grant pardon to the King.

units.la: Ergo adorant creaturam inanimatam, quia prototypon, nempe crux in qua Christus pependit, non fuit adoranda.
units.tr: Therefore they adore an inanimate creature, since the prototype, namely the cross on which Christ hung, was not to be adored.

units.la: Tertiò, excusatio Harscheri nulla est, quia magni viri ex pontificiis statuunt imagini & exemplari eundem honorem exhiberi. De quibus videatur Bellarm. lib. II. de eccl. triumph. cap. 20.
units.tr: Third, Harscher's excuse is worth nothing, because great men among the Papists hold that the same honour is shown to the image and to its exemplar. On this see Bellarmine, book II, De ecclesia triumphante, chap. 20.

units.la: Et Bellarminus cap. sequenti statim, a principio hanc habet propositionem: imagines Christi & sanctorum venerandæ sunt, non solum per accidens & impropriè, sed etiam per se & propriè, ita ut ipsæ terminent venerationem, ut in se considerantur, & non solum ut vicem gerunt exemplaris. Verum quidem est, ipsos hoc dissimulare coram populo, suadente Bellarmino ne offendant aures catholicorum, imprimis fi dicatur imagines adorandas esse adoratione eadem latriæ,duliæ & hyperduliæ cum exemplari, quod quidam ex pontificiis faciunt, ut Thomas, Bonaventura, Cajetanus & alii, quod putat fieri magno cum periculo. Sed quale periculum? Polydorus, Virgilius testatur, bene multos rudiores esse, qui imagines colunt, non ut figuras, sed ut senjum aliquem habentes, majorem fiduciam in iis collocare quàm in ipso Christo. lib. 6. cap. 13.
units.tr: And Bellarmine, immediately in the following chapter, begins with this proposition: The images of Christ and of the saints are to be venerated not only accidentally and improperly, but also per se and properly, so that they themselves terminate the veneration, as they are considered in themselves, and not only as they take the place of the exemplar. It is true indeed that they conceal this before the people, Bellarmine advising that they not offend the ears of Catholics, especially if it is said that images are to be adored with the same adoration of latria, dulia and hyperdulia as the exemplar, which some of the Papists do, such as Thomas, Bonaventure, Cajetan and others, which they think is done at great risk. But what risk? Polydore Vergil testifies that there are many rather simple people who worship images, not as figures, but as having some divinity, and who place greater trust in them than in Christ himself. Book 6, chap. 13.

units.la: {Q}Quarto, concedatur, ipsos imagines adorare ut sunt signa amicorum Dei, tamen est idololatria. Etenim idololatria non est æstimanda ex obiecto, sed obiecti falso usu, cum res quæ Deus non est, vice Dei colitur, ita ut fiduciam in illam colloces. Sol & Luna res sunt per se bonæ, & ad bonû usum creatæ, quia autem Ethnici ad cultum iis abutebantur, idololatriam commisisse dicuntur. Herodes ex seipso idolum fecit, quando permisit ut populus ipsi acclamaret; vox Dei & non hominis, Act. 12:25. Et Apostolus eodem sensu avarum vocat idololatram, Eph.5:5. Sic ergo sancti demortui fiunt idola pontificiis, nullo tamen sanctorum vitio, qui hunc cultum reiecerunt, Act. 10:26. Apoc.19:10. Unde Cyrill. Alexand. lib. II. Thesau. c.1. Sic primum in idololatriam incides, cum Dominum verum non fateris, adoresque illum quem Deo Patri consubstantialem esse non credas, sed potius creaturam. Distinctio latriae, duliae & hyperduliae autores habuit in scripturis sacris & lingua graeca parum exercitatos.
units.tr: Fourthly, grant that they adore images as signs of God's friends; it is still idolatry. For idolatry is not to be judged by its object but by the false use of the object, when a thing that is not God is worshipped in God's place, so that you place your trust in it. The sun and moon are things good in themselves and created for a good use, yet because the heathen abused them for worship, they are said to have committed idolatry. Herod made an idol of himself when he allowed the people to shout to him, the voice of God and not of man (Acts 12:25). And the Apostle in the same sense calls the covetous man an idolater (Eph. 5:5). So the dead saints become idols for the Papists, though not through any fault of the saints, who rejected such worship (Acts 10:26; Rev. 19:10). Hence Cyril of Alexandria, Thesaurus bk. 2, ch. 1: Thus you first fall into idolatry when you do not confess the true Lord, and worship him whom you do not believe to be consubstantial with God the Father, but rather a creature. The distinction between latria, dulia and hyperdulia has its authors in men little practised in the holy Scriptures and in the Greek tongue.

units.la: Calvinus lib. IV. Instit. c. 7. not. 27. scribit Pontificem cum Cardinalibus docere nullum esse Deum, nullum Christum, nullam resurrectionem. Inquit Harscherus.
units.tr: Calvin, Institutes bk. 4, ch. 7, note 27, writes that the Pope with the Cardinals teaches that there is no God, no Christ, no resurrection. So says Harscher.

units.la: Calvinus in cap. 7. lib. IV. Instit. disputat de vicariatu Christi & primatu, & parag. 24. negavit episcopum Romanum esse episcoporum principem, quod eodem parag. & sequentibus duobus ex reipsa probavit. Paragrapho vero 27. ad personas ipsas venit pontificum Romanorum de quibus ita scribit: Ad homines autem si veniamus satis scitur, quales reperturi simus Christi vicarios. Iulius scilicet & Leo & Clemens & Paulus, Christiana fidei columnae erunt, primi religionis interpretes, qui nihil aliud de Christo tenuerunt, nisi quod didicerant in schola Luciani. Sed quid tres aut quatuor pontifices enumero? Quasi vero dubium sit qualem religionem professi sint jam pridem pontifices cum toto Cardinalium collegio & hodie profiteantur. Primum enim arcana illius Theologia, quae inter eos regnat, caput est, nullum esse Deum; Alterum, quaecunque de Christo scripta sunt ac docentur, mendacia esse & impostura. Tertium, doctrinam de futura vita & ultima resurrectione meras esse fabulas. Non omnes ita sentiunt pauci ita loquuntur. Fateor: jam pridem tamen hæc ordinaria esse cepit pontificum religio. Hæc sunt verba Calvini. Ubi sciendum Calvinum hæc non ex odio erga pontifices Romanos, sed propter historiæ veritatem dixisse. Quia tales revera reperti sunt, ut hoc loco scribit Calvinus. Homines palam impii, truculenti, incæstuosi, &c. Hi dicuntur Deum negare, ab Apostolo Juda, v. 4. Impij, qui Dei nostri gratiam transferunt ad lascivniam, & solum illum verum Deum, ac Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum negant.
units.tr: Calvin, in ch. 7 of bk. 4 of the Institutes, discusses the vicariate and primacy of Christ, and in section 24 denies that the Roman bishop is the prince of bishops, which in the same section and the two following he proves from the facts themselves. In section 27 he comes to the persons of the Roman pontiffs, of whom he writes thus: If we come to the men themselves, it is well known what kind of Christ's vicars we shall find. Julius, Leo, Clement and Paul, forsooth, will be the pillars of the Christian faith, the first interpreters of religion, who held nothing about Christ except what they had learned in the school of Lucian. But why do I enumerate three or four pontiffs? As if it were doubtful what religion the pontiffs, together with the whole college of Cardinals, have long professed and profess today. For the first secret of that theology which reigns among them is that there is no God; the second, that whatever is written and taught about Christ is lies and imposture; the third, that the doctrine of the future life and the final resurrection is mere fables. Not all think so, few speak so openly. I grant it: yet this religion of the pontiffs has long since begun to be the ordinary one. These are Calvin's words. Here it must be noted that Calvin said these things not out of hatred for the Roman pontiffs, but for the sake of historical truth. For such men were indeed found, as Calvin writes in this place: men openly impious, savage, incestuous, and so on. These are said to deny God, according to the Apostle Jude, v. 4: ungodly men, who turn the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and deny the only true God and our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.la: Leo Decimus, Machiavellicæ doctrinæ innutritus & plane deditus, doctrinam de Christo reputavit pro mero figmento: articulū de vita æterna pro nænijs, quibus in officio contineretur vulgus: se mirari dixit quod regnum sacerdotale tam diu subsistere potuerit, quod meris nugis niteretur.
units.tr: Leo X, nourished on Machiavellian doctrine and wholly given over to it, regarded the doctrine about Christ as pure fiction, and the article about eternal life as trifles by which the common people were kept in their duty; he said he wondered that the priestly kingdom could have lasted so long, when it rested on mere nonsense.

units.la: Iulius Secundus, qui nominandus suisset truculentus, clavibus Petri in Tiberim proiectis, fe gladium Pauli arripuisse dixit, quo in prœliis uteretur: quo etiam intra feptennium 200000. homines cum milite Româ educto, trucidavit.
units.tr: Julius II, who ought to be named the savage, after casting the keys of Peter into the Tiber, said he had seized the sword of Paul to use in battles; with it, too, within seven years he slaughtered 200,000 men, having led them out of Rome with the soldiery.

units.la: Paulus Tertius, matrem veneno suffulit, Lauram Farnesiam ex fratre nepte inceftu polluit, ut & filiam suam Constantiam marito ereptam: Christum ludibrio habuit, Bembo Cardinali dicere solitus: o Bembe, Bembe, quantum nobis profuit fabula de Christo.
units.tr: Paul III supported his mother with poison, polluted Laura Farnese, his niece by his brother, with incest, and likewise snatched his daughter Constance from her husband. He made a mockery of Christ, being accustomed to say to Cardinal Bembo: O Bembo, Bembo, how much profit we have got from the fable about Christ!

units.la: Iohannes XXIII. resurrectionem mortuorum negavit. De his locutus est Calvinus, sed ita locutus, ut tamen addat, jam pridem hæc ordinaria esse cepit Pontificum religio, quia historiæ ipsæ Calvino ignotæ non fuerunt, quæ nobis describunt vitam & actiones Pontificum, Alexandri VI. Johannis XXII. Johannis XXIII. Johannis XIII. Johannis XII. & aliorum. Nam paucos commemoravi. Baronius ad annum 897. fuisse intrusos in cathedram Petri & solium Christi, homines monstrosos, vitâ turpissimos, moribus perditissimos, usq; quaq; foedissimos. Videatur etiam Platina in vita Sergii III.
units.tr: John XXIII denied the resurrection of the dead. Calvin spoke of these men, but in such a way as to add, this religion of the pontiffs has long since begun to be the ordinary one, because the histories which describe for us the lives and deeds of the pontiffs, of Alexander VI, John XXII, John XXIII, John XIII, John XII and others, were not unknown to Calvin. For I have mentioned only a few. Baronius, at the year 897, says that monstrous men, most vile in life, most depraved in morals, and in every way most foul, were thrust into the chair of Peter and the throne of Christ. Platina, in the life of Sergius III, may also be consulted.

units.la: Nec video cur vel Calvinus vel alii, qui hæc Romanistis obiiciunt, mendacii accusari possint, quandoquidem illi nihil nisi quod ex historiis ab ipsis Pontificiis conscriptis, hïc proferant.
units.tr: Nor do I see why either Calvin or others who throw these things in the teeth of the Romanists can be accused of lying, since they bring forward nothing here except what is taken from histories written by the Papists themselves.

units.la: Atquè huc facit quod infra de libello quodam germanico scribit HarschErus, cuius titulus est, Die Himlische Scheidung &c. In quo author (quisquis ille fuerit, Italum esse credo nam primò Italicè conscriptus cum titulo Il divortio celeste) Urbani VIII. actiones describit sub continua allegoria. Sed quis est qui ignoret illa tempora? testabuntur Cardinales Hispanici, testabitur Roma, & princeps Parmensis, aliiquè plures. Ego verò librum illum non defendo, non enim omnia in eo mihi placent, nec autor mihi notus. Imo non credo hominem fuisse confessionis orthodoxae, sed Italum cui clericorum mores maxime displicebant, quales multi sunt ex Pontificiis. Quod sic credam, in causa est, quia nemo nostrum scribit aut sentit, Deum aut Christum sponsam suam, id est, ecclesiam abiecisse. Absit hoc, ut ecclesia sanguine Dei redempta, unice a Deo dilecta, abiiciatur. Quocirca nos in ista materia nunquam non cum scriptura loquimur. Quanquam enim Elias ad Deum clamavit dicendo; Israelita dereliquerunt fedus tuum, altaria tua destruxerunt, & prophetas tuos occiderunt gladio, atque ego relictus sum solus, tamen Deus ecclesiam suam non abiecit, reservans sibi adhuc septies mille ex Israele, 1. Reg. 19: 14, 15. Quanquam Deus populum Israeliticum propter incredulitatem abiecit, & defracti sunt etiam rami naturales: tamen Deus non abjecit populum suum, quem praenovit, quia reservatio facta est secundum electionem gratuitam. Rom. II: 2, 5. Ita quoque quamvis ecclesia hodierna Romana a fide defecerit & quâ talis non sit sponsa Christi, cuius vocem non audit, tamen Deus non abiecit ecclesiam suam, sed in defectrice ecclesia habuit populum suum, quem iussit exire ex Babylone, ne particeps fiat peccatorum ejus. Apoc. 18: 4.
units.tr: To this point also is what Harscher writes below about a certain German booklet, whose title is Die Himlische Scheidung (The Heavenly Divorce), etc. In it the author (whoever he was; I believe he was an Italian, since it was first written in Italian under the title Il divortio celeste) describes the deeds of Urban VIII under a continuous allegory. But who is there who does not know those times? The Spanish Cardinals will bear witness, Rome will bear witness, and the Prince of Parma, and many others. As for myself, I do not defend that book; not everything in it pleases me, nor is its author known to me. Indeed I do not believe he was a man of orthodox confession, but an Italian whom the morals of the clergy displeased most, of which kind there are many among the Papists. That I believe this is because none of us writes or thinks that God or Christ has cast off his bride, that is, the Church. Far be it: that the Church, redeemed by the blood of God and loved by God alone, should be cast off. Wherefore in this matter we never speak except from Scripture. For although Elijah cried out to God, saying: The Israelites have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, yet God did not cast off his Church, reserving for himself seven thousand from Israel (1 Kings 19:14, 15). Although God cast off the Israelite people because of unbelief, and the natural branches were also broken off, yet God did not cast off his people whom he foreknew, because the remnant was made according to gracious election (Rom. 11:2, 5). So too, although the present Roman Church has fallen away from the faith and as such is not the bride of Christ, whose voice she does not hear, yet God has not cast off his Church, but in the defecting Church he has had his people, whom he commanded to come out of Babylon, that you may not share in her sins (Rev. 18:4).

units.la: Quàm inepta ergo ista: & haec sunt motiva fidei reformatae ecclesiae, qualis ergo ipsa fides his fundamentis confirmata? scilicet ex falsis & alienis sententiis fidem nostram iniustè traducere est Theologum agere.
units.tr: How foolish, then, is that: and these are the motives of the reformed Church's faith; what then is the faith itself, confirmed on such foundations? Clearly, to unjustly traduce our faith on the basis of false and alien opinions is to play the theologian badly.

units.la: Sed accedo ad accusationem mihi noti Domini Crespei, de quo ita scribit Harscherus: In hoc mendacio egregiè succollavit Calvino Iacobus Crespei, qui in sua declaratione fidei, quam Bernae fecit & imprimi curavit non veritus est scribere, in imagine Georgÿ equus una adoratur cum suo Domino: in imagine Anthonij porcus participat candelas æque ac ipse Anthonius, bos & asinus cum virginis Mariæ & Iosephi imaginibus adorantur. In imagine Michaëlis Diabolus unà cum Michaële spectatur erectus, nec minus ille quàm ipse à miseris papistis adoratur. Ad hæc Harscherus: ô hominis improbi decumana mendacia, juxta quæ nulla fides boni viri consistat. Sed bona verba quæso. Voluit Dominus Crespeus, qui in Academia Valentiana ultra triginta annos Theologiæ Doctor & celebris Professor fuit, describere summam miseriam & crassissimum errorem populi in Papatu viventis, eò quòd adorent res, quæ aures habent & non audiunt, os & non loquuntur, oculos & non vident. Id fecit ex descriptione actionum circa imagines. Adduxit quatuor exempla, imaginem Gegorii cum equo, Anthonii cum porco, B. virginis & Iosephi cum bove & asino, Michaëlis cum Diabolo, & docuit hæc indistinctè adorari à miseris papistis. Ubi vocem adorationis accepit pro externo actu corporis, genuflectione, incurvatione & capitis detectione quomodo saepius in scriptura accipitur, ut Gen. 23: 7 ubi dicitur, Abraham se incurvasse coram populo Cheti, septuaginta habent προσεκύνησε τῷ λαῷ τῆς γῆς, Vulgatus, adoravit populum terrae. Et Gen 33: 3. dicitur Jacobus septies se incurvasse coram Esavo. Septuaginta iterum; καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτὸν ἑπτάκις. Vulgatus, & adoravit super terram septies. Vult ergo Dominus Crespeus illam incurvationem & genuflectionem, quam Pontificii exhibent imaginibus pariter fieri coram porco & Anthonio, pariter coram equo & Georgio, pariter coram Michaele & Diabolo &c. Quamvis forte intentio cultus religiosi fiat respectu imaginum Anthonii & Michaelis &c. In eo vero ridiculus est Pater Harscher quod scribit, mendacium esse decumanum quod in imagine Anthony porcus aque participet
units.tr: But I come to the accusation of my acquaintance Lord Crespey, about whom Harscher writes thus: In this lie Jacques Crespey has ably supported Calvin, who in his declaration of faith, which he made and had printed at Bern, did not hesitate to write that in the picture of George a horse is adored along with its lord; in the picture of Anthony a pig shares in the candles just as Anthony himself does; an ox and an ass are adored together with the images of the Virgin Mary and Joseph. In the picture of Michael the Devil is seen standing erect beside Michael, and is adored by the wretched Papists no less than Michael himself. To this Harscher adds: O the shameless, sweeping lies of this man, on which no good man's faith could stand. But, I beg, let us use fair words. Lord Crespey, who at the Academy of Valencia was a Doctor of Theology and celebrated Professor for more than thirty years, wished to describe the great misery and gross error of the people living in the Papacy, in that they adore things that have ears and do not hear, mouths and do not speak, eyes and do not see. He did this from a description of the acts performed before images. He adduced four examples: the picture of George with his horse, of Anthony with his pig, of the Blessed Virgin and Joseph with the ox and ass, and of Michael with the Devil, and he taught that these are adored indiscriminately by the wretched Papists. Here he took the word adoration for an outward bodily act, a genuflection, a bowing and an uncovering of the head, in the sense in which it is more often used in Scripture, as in Gen. 23:7, where it is said that Abraham bowed himself before the people of Heth; the Seventy have prosekynēse tō laō tēs gēs [προσεκύνησε τῷ λαῷ τῆς γῆς], the Vulgate adored the people of the land. And at Gen. 33:3 it is said that Jacob bowed himself seven times before Esau. The Seventy again: kai prosekynēsen auton heptakis [καὶ προσεκύνησεν αὐτὸν ἑπτάκις]; the Vulgate, and adored upon the earth seven times. Lord Crespey therefore means that the bowing and genuflection which the Papists make before images is equally made before the pig and Anthony, equally before the horse and George, equally before Michael and the Devil, and so on; although perhaps the intention of religious worship is directed to the images of Anthony and Michael, and so on. But in this Father Harscher is ridiculous, in that he writes that it is a sweeping lie that in the picture of Anthony a pig shares in the candles

units.la: K candelas, ac ipsa Anthonij imago, seu ipse Anthonius. Edoceat ergo nos utrum magis videat ex appositis candelis, imago Anthonii, an imago porci.
units.tr: Candles, and the very image of Anthony, or Anthony himself. Let him therefore teach us whether the image of Anthony or the image of the pig is what is more plainly seen from the candles placed before it.

units.la: Sed haec non tantopere stomachum movissent Harschero, si medicamentum sumpsisset ex Vasquesii Jesuitae officina, qui in tertia part. Thom. disput. 110. q. 2. docet, quamlibet creaturam in mundo sive inanimatam & irrationalem, sive rationalem ex natura rei, & secluso periculo, rite cum Deo sicut imago ipsius adorari posse. Et hoc esse eximia religionis opus. Vide quousque tandem devenerit irreligiosa illa philosophia papistica.
units.tr: But these things would not have so greatly stirred Harscher's bile if he had taken his medicine from the workshop of the Jesuit Vasquez, who in the third part of Thomas, disputation 110, question 2, teaches that any creature in the world, whether inanimate and irrational or rational by nature, may rightly be adored with God as his image, provided there is no danger. And this is a distinguished work of religion. See how far that irreligious papistical philosophy has at last gone.

units.la: Obiicit porrò: Quin ejusdem Crespei declaratio fidei tota in eo est, ut ostendat catholicos esse tyrannos, non in homines sed in ipsum Christum Deum, esse Idololatras, esse Magos. Hoc est ipsius symbolum Apostolicum, Nicenum, Constantinopolitanum, Athanasianum, hoc purum putum Evangelium, hac fidei apostolica reformatio, credo papistas esse in Christum Deum tyrannos, credo papistas esse idololatras, credo papistas esse Magos. Pro fidem reformatam! in cujus professione ne unicum ex symbolo apostolico continetur articulus.
units.tr: He objects further: Indeed the whole of this Crespe's declaration of faith consists in showing that Catholics are tyrants, not over men but over Christ himself, God; that they are idolaters and magicians. This is his Apostles' creed, his Nicene, Constantinopolitan and Athanasian creed; this is the pure and simple Gospel, this is the reformation of the apostolic faith: I believe that the papists are tyrants against Christ God, I believe that the papists are idolaters, I believe that the papists are magicians. O reformed faith! In whose profession not even a single article of the Apostles' creed is contained.

units.la: Scribit, in declaratione fidei reformata Crespei ne unicum contineri articulum symboli apostolici. Sed primo, non est professio seu confessio fidei D. Crespei, nec titulus ita habet, sed declaratio fidei circa articulos nempe praecipuos fidei, quos tenet ipse, & quos Pontificii multifariè corruperunt. Secundo salsum est, quod nulli articulii fidei in illa declaratione continentur. En sequentes pag. 5. Scriptura sacra nos docent, unico Christi sacrificio in cruce perac-to, omnia nostra peccata penitus deleta fuisse, nobisq; Deum redditum fuisse propitium, atq; ita nullum superesse locum ulli alteri sacrificio propitiatorio, Heb. 10: 14. cap. 9: 28. Col. 2: 14. pag. 6. Scriptura docet, Christum se pro nobis obtulisse Deo, quia mortuus est pro nobis. Hi duo articuli habentur in symbolo Apostolico & reliquis symbolis, cùm credimus, Christum passum esse sub Pontio Pilato, crucifixum & mortuum. Pagniâ cådem, scriptura nos docet, invocandum esse solum Deum, nec alium quærendum mediatorem, quàm unicum Iesum Christum. Item ibid. Atqui in symbolo docemur, in Patrem Filium & Spiritum sanctum credere. Hi continentur in symbolo Apostolico cùm dicimus; Credo in Deum Patrem omnipotentem creatorem cœli & terræ. Et in Jesum Christum Filium eius unicum Dominum nostrum. Credo in Spiritum sanctum. pag. 7. Christus perfectissimus noster redemptor & mediator nobis vitam æternam perfectissimè promeritus est. Sic omnes Prophetæ, sic Apostoli crediderunt, ut Petrus testatur Act. 4: 12.
units.tr: He writes that in Crespe's reformed declaration of faith not a single article of the Apostles' creed is contained. But first, this is not a profession or confession of faith by Master Crespe, nor does its title read so; it is a declaration of faith concerning the chief articles of faith, which he himself holds and which the Papists have corrupted in many ways. Second, it is false that no articles of faith are contained in that declaration. Note the following, on page 5: The Holy Scriptures teach us that by the one sacrifice of Christ on the cross, accomplished once, all our sins have been wholly blotted out, and God has been made propitious to us, and thus that no place remains for any other propitiatory sacrifice (Heb. 10:14; ch. 9:28; Col. 2:14). On page 6: Scripture teaches that Christ offered himself to God for us, because he died for us. These two articles are found in the Apostles' creed and the other creeds, when we believe that Christ suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified and died. On the same page: Scripture teaches us that God alone is to be invoked, and that no mediator is to be sought other than the one Jesus Christ. Likewise, in the same place: But in the creed we are taught to believe in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. These are contained in the Apostles' creed when we say: I believe in God the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth; and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord; I believe in the Holy Spirit. On page 7: Christ, our most perfect redeemer and mediator, has most perfectly merited eternal life for us. So all the prophets, so the apostles believed, as Peter testifies, Acts 4:12.

units.la: Reliqua quæ addidit, utpote: Pontifices esse tyrannos, item papistas esse Idololatras & Magos, gos, non pari fide credidit. Priora fide iustificante, posteriora fide historica. Nam non illico, si ego credam Harscherum esse Jesuitam, item; Friburgi esse collegium Jesuiticum, hi sunt articuli fidei meæ per quos ego cupiam salvari. Quantæ hæ ineptiæ! Præterea quòd sic sensit D. Crespeus, suas habuit rationes, in declaratione fidei propositas. Cur Harscherus illas non refutavit?
units.tr: As for the rest that he added, namely: that the popes are tyrants, likewise that the papists are idolaters and magicians, he did not believe these with the same faith. The former he believes with justifying faith, the latter with historical faith. For it does not follow at once that, if I believe Harscher to be a Jesuit, and that there is a Jesuit college at Freiburg, these are articles of my faith through which I desire to be saved. How foolish these things are! Moreover, that Crespe so thought, he had his reasons, which he set out in his declaration of faith. Why did Harscher not refute them?

units.la: Quartus articulus, in quo etiam concordant universi sectarij, scilicet quòd sit papistica carnificina & impietas 1. enumerare & confiteri peccata. 2. satisfactionem, quâ pœna temporaria mitigetur suscipere. 3. bonis operibus ex Divinæ gratiæ & meritorum Christi virtute profectis vitam æternam velle mereri. 4. quòd confirmatio, matrimonium, extrema unctio humana inventa sint, non sacramenta ecclesiæ.
units.tr: The fourth article, in which all the sectaries also agree, namely that it is papistical butchery and impiety (1) to enumerate and confess sins; (2) to undertake satisfaction, by which temporal punishment is mitigated; (3) to wish to merit eternal life by good works proceeding from the power of divine grace and the merits of Christ; (4) that confirmation, matrimony and extreme unction are human inventions, not sacraments of the Church.

units.la: 1. Confessionem peccatorum necessariam esse confitemur, quæ fit Deo, ecclesiæ clesiæ, Episcopo & proximo. De hac disputabimus prolixius ad controversiam primam seculi VI. quando Harscherus in Hæresi Jacobinorum quæsrit; An sacerdoti omnia peccata mortalia sint confessione exponenda?
units.tr: (1) We confess that confession of sins is necessary; it is made to God, to the Church, to the bishop and to the neighbour. We shall dispute about this at greater length at the first controversy of the sixth century, when Harscher asks, in his Heresy of the Jacobins: Must all mortal sins be laid open to the priest in confession?

units.la: 2. Satisfactionem, quâ pœna temporaria mitigetur, suscipere esse impietatem.
units.tr: 2. That to undertake satisfaction, by which temporal punishment is mitigated, is impiety.

units.la: Non est quæstio de politica satisfactione, quâ quis propter damnum & iniurias Magistratui vel proximo illatas secundùm leges punitur, & sic legibus, proximoquè satisfacit. Quomodo in V. T. fur, qui furatus est bovem rependere debebat quinquè boves, & pro una pecude quatuor pecudes, quò pertinent mulctæ pecuniariæ & omnis generis supplicia; sed de satisfactione ecclesiastica & canonica. Ea autem est vel veteris & primitivæ ecclesiæ, vel novæ papisticæ.
units.tr: The question is not about political satisfaction, by which someone is punished according to the laws for damage and injuries inflicted on the magistrate or on a neighbour, and so makes satisfaction to the laws and to the neighbour. Thus in the Old Testament a thief who had stolen an ox had to restore five oxen, and for one sheep four sheep; to this belong monetary fines and every kind of punishment. But the question is about ecclesiastical and canonical satisfaction. This is either that of the ancient and primitive Church, or that of the new papistical Church.

units.la: Veteris & primitivæ ecclesiæ satisfactio erat, cùm illi, qui gravissimè magnoquè gnoque cum ecclesiæ scandalo peccarunt, legibus & canonibus ab ecclesia præscriptis satisfecerunt. Istæ satisfactiones erant poenæ canonicæ, Græcè τὰ ἐπιτίμια dictæ, de quibus Basilius Magnus & Cyprianus consulendi. Per hoc enim ecclesia, experimentum fecit, an serio poenitentiam egissent excommunicati. Unde Augustinus dicit, Enchir. ad Laur. cap. 65. debere ecclesiæ fieri satis.
units.tr: The satisfaction of the ancient and primitive Church was this: when those who had sinned most grievously and to the great scandal of the Church made satisfaction according to the laws and canons prescribed by the Church. These satisfactions were called canonical penances, in Greek epitimia [τὰ ἐπιτίμια], on which Basil the Great and Cyprian should be consulted. For through this the Church made trial whether the excommunicated had seriously undertaken repentance. Hence Augustine says, in the Enchiridion to Laurentius, chapter 65, that satisfaction ought to be made to the Church.

units.la: Tertullianus etiam satisfactionem Dei appellat respectu mandati Christi, Matth. 18: 17, 18. quia Dominus vult ut audiatur ecclesia. Lib. de poenit. cap. 10. hæ satisfactiones quæ non erant redemptionis poenæ temporariæ, sed ritus & actiones testandæ poenitentiæ causâ ab ecclesia præceptæ & à peccatoribus suscepta, magnum habebant usum. Nam inde ecclesia judicium fecit & experimentum poenitentiæ, ut ante dixi. Deinde alii huiusmodi exemplo territi, didicerunt in confessione fidei & pietate perseverare, ipsi vero peccatores in posterum a peccatis abstinere. Hi fuerunt satisfactionis ecclesiasticæ fines, neutiquam vero ut essent meritoriæ coram tribunali Dei. Atque hanc satisfactionem ecclesiasticam tanquam utilem approbamus.
units.tr: Tertullian too calls it satisfaction to God with respect to the command of Christ (Matt. 18:17, 18), because the Lord wills that the Church be heard. Book on repentance, chapter 10. These satisfactions, which were not a redemption of temporal punishment, but rites and actions enjoined by the Church for the sake of attesting repentance and undertaken by the sinners, had great use. For thereby the Church formed a judgement and a trial of repentance, as I said before. Then others, terrified by such an example, learned to persevere in the confession of faith and in piety, and the sinners themselves to abstain from sins in future. These were the purposes of ecclesiastical satisfaction, but by no means that they should be meritorious before the judgement seat of God. And we approve this ecclesiastical satisfaction as useful.

units.la: Satisfactio ecclesiæ novæ papisticæ a priori toto cœlo distat, & partim ex Concilio Tridentino sess. XIV. partim ex aliis authoribus definiri potest, quâ homo, qui mortaliter peccavit, post consessionem sacerdoti factam, opera pœnalia indicta ab alio vel sponte suscepta, præstat, utpote orationes, ieiunia, eleemosynas, vigilias, peregrinationes & disciplinam corporis, ut post culpam remissam, Deo satisfaciant pro pœna temporali.
units.tr: The satisfaction of the new papistical Church differs from the former toto cœlo, and may be defined partly from the Council of Trent, session 14, partly from other authors, as: that by which a man who has sinned mortally, after confession made to a priest, performs penitential works imposed by another or undertaken of his own accord, such as prayers, fasts, alms, vigils, pilgrimages and bodily discipline, so that, after the guilt is remitted, they may satisfy God for the temporal punishment.

units.la: Primò differt à veteris ecclesiæ satisfactionibus, quia illæ nec multæ pecuniariæ, nec actus poenales fuerunt, sed disciplina ecclesiastica tantùm, & satisfactiones ecclesiæ propter scandalum lum offensæ: & consistebant in quibusdam ceremoniis ad terrendos peccatores institutis. Utpote quòd peccator primò ad tempus debebat stare ἐξω τῆς πύλης τῆς ἀυκτηρίας (extra portam oratorii) & cum fletu introeuntes rogare, ut pro se precentur. Secundò absoluto tempore τῆς ὑποπλαυσεως, admittebatur ἐντὸς τῆς πύλης ἐν τῷ ναρθηκι, intra portam in porticum, ad auditionem scripturarum & doctrinæ usquè ad catechumenos, sed postmodum iussus egredi, nec dignus censebatur precatione. Tertiò permissum ei stare ἑστῶτα τῆς πύλης τῆς ναῦ intra portam templi, ubi prostratus pœnitentiam egit, hoc vocabant admitti εἰς μετάνοιαν. Quartò denique concessum pervenire ad congregationem fidelium, & cum ipsis subsistere nec cum catechumenis egredi. Ubi hæc præscripto tempore & modo præstitit, dictum fuit satisfactum est, & denuò admittebatur ad μετάσχειν τῶν ἁγιασμάτων, ad participationem sacramentorum. Hæc leguntur apud Gregorium Neocæsariensem.
units.tr: First, it differs from the satisfactions of the ancient Church, because those were neither monetary fines nor penal acts, but only ecclesiastical discipline, and satisfactions for the scandal of the offence; and they consisted in certain ceremonies instituted to terrify sinners. For instance, the sinner had first, for a time, to stand outside the gate of the oratory [ἔξω τῆς πύλης τῆς εὐκτηρίας] and, as those entering passed by, to beg them with tears to pray for him. Second, after the period of hypopausis [τῆς ὑποπλαυσεως] had elapsed, he was admitted within the gate, in the narthex [ἐντὸς τῆς πύλης ἐν τῷ νάρθηκι], inside the gate into the porch, to hear the Scriptures and the teaching, as far as the catechumens, but was afterwards bidden to go out, and was not deemed worthy of prayer. Third, he was permitted to stand within the gate of the nave [ἑστῶτα τῆς πύλης τῆς ναῦ], inside the gate of the temple, where, prostrate, he performed penance; this they called being admitted to repentance [εἰς μετάνοιαν]. Fourth and finally, he was granted to come to the assembly of the faithful, and to stand with them, not to go out with the catechumens. When he had performed these things in the prescribed time and manner, it was said satisfaction has been made, and he was admitted again to partake of the holy things [μετάσχειν τῶν ἁγιασμάτων], to the participation of the sacraments. These things are read in Gregory of Neocaesarea.

units.la: In hisce omnibus nihil aliud quæsiverunt, quam seriam & veram poenitentiam & cordis contritionem, quam ex hisce actionibus, sicuti etiam ex ieiuniis, cilicibus, sacco, colligere poterant. Unde Cyprianus: satisfactio est agnitio culpæ & venia deprecatio. Interim ad maiorem huius tam necessariæ poenitentiæ commendationem sæpe dixerunt, opera pœnitentia peccatum tollere, lachrymis peccata purgari, eleemosynas peccata mundare, non quidem meritorie & expiatorie (nam sanguis Iesu Christi purgat nos ab Omni Peccato) sed quia media sunt quibus actus purgatorij abrumpuntur & peccatores emendantur. Quomodo omnes ipsorum phrases sunt intelligendæ.
units.tr: In all these things they sought nothing other than serious and true repentance and contrition of heart, which they could gather from these actions, as also from fasts, hair shirts and sackcloth. Hence Cyprian: satisfaction is the acknowledgement of guilt and the seeking of pardon. Meanwhile, to commend more highly this so necessary repentance, they often said that works of repentance remove sin, sins are purged by tears, alms cleanse sins, not indeed meritoriously and expiatorily (for the blood of Jesus Christ cleanses us from all sin), but because they are means by which the acts of purgatory are cut short and sinners are amended. In this way all their phrases are to be understood.

units.la: Satisfactiones vero in ecclesia Romana hodierna longe aliter sese habent. Nam primo absolutio non sequitur satisfactiones ut olim, sed eas praecedit. Secundo, volunt satisfactiones illas esse iustitiae Christi-cooperativas & eius veluti supplementum.
units.tr: Yet in the present-day Roman Church the satisfactions stand in a very different position. For, first, absolution does not follow satisfactions as it once did, but comes before them. Second, they want these satisfactions to cooperate with the righteousness of Christ and to serve as its supplement.

units.la: Tertio fingunt hisce operibus poenalibus tanquam propriis meritis gloriam aeternam acquiri & possideri veluti altero titulo, ut loquitur Bellarminus.
units.tr: Third, they imagine that by these penal works, as if they were their own merits, eternal glory is acquired and possessed, as it were by another title, to use Bellarmine's expression.

units.la: Quarto posse aliquem in hisce satisfactionibus ultra propriam perfectionem pervenire, ita ut pro aliis quoque sive in hac vita, sive in purgatorio existentibus satisfacere possit. Quod horrendum monstrum veteribus fuit inauditum.
units.tr: Fourth, they hold that someone can by these satisfactions go beyond his own perfection, so that he can also make satisfaction for others, whether they are still living in this life or are in purgatory. This horrible monster was unknown to the ancients.

units.la: Quinto indulgentias excogitarunt, quibus licet quis non satisfaciat pro peccatis suis, tamen pro pecunia remissionem omnium peccatorum non tantum praeteritorum, sed aliquando etiam suturorum acquirere potest. Quod totam naturam poenitentiae tollit.
units.tr: Fifth, they have devised indulgences, by which a man, though he does not satisfy for his own sins, can nevertheless acquire for money the remission not only of past sins but sometimes even of future ones. This destroys the whole nature of repentance.

units.la: Sexto habent coniunctas duas salsissimas hypothefes, 1. quod peccata alia sint mortalia alia venialia, idque ex sua natura. 2. quòd remissâ culpâ remaneat adhuc pœna solvenda, pro qua homines Deo satisfacere teneantur. Quasi homo pœna dignus sit, licèt non sit culpabilis.
units.tr: Sixth, they join together two most absurd suppositions: (1) that some sins are mortal and others venial, and this by their very nature; (2) that after the guilt is forgiven, a punishment still remains to be paid, for which men are bound to make satisfaction to God. As if a man deserved punishment although he is not guilty.

units.la: Atquè hæc omnia quia vetustati, veritati, sacræ scripturæ, & imprimis sanctissimæ & sufficientissimæ satisfactioni Christi contrariantur, dicimus, sententiam de satisfactionibus hodiernis Romanis impiam & blasphemam esse.
units.tr: Since all these things are contrary to antiquity, to truth, to Holy Scripture, and above all to the most holy and most sufficient satisfaction of Christ, we say that the opinion on present-day Roman satisfactions is impious and blasphemous.

units.la: III. Bonis operibus, ex divina gratia & meritorum Christi virtute profectis, vitam æternam velle mereri, esse impium.
units.tr: III. That to wish to merit eternal life by good works, which proceed from divine grace and the virtue of Christ's merits, is impious.

units.la: Per bona opera, ex virtute divinæ gratiæ, merito Christi impetratæ, fideles ad vitam æternam pervenire, & absque his neminem eò pertingere posse fatemur; quòd autem propterea vitam æternam mereantur, negamus.
units.tr: We confess that the faithful attain eternal life through good works, which come from the power of divine grace obtained by the merit of Christ, and that no one can reach it without these; but we deny that they therefore merit eternal life.

units.la: Nam 1. Scriptura sacra ne unicum locum habet, in quo reperiatur vox meritum aut mereri. Locus Heb. 13: 16. in græco habet ἀδάρεσιν, quod rectius per delectatur redditur, sicuti etiam vulgatus ἀδάρεσον & ἀδαρεσεόμαι per placitum & placere reddidit Col. 3:20. Filii, obedite parentibus per omnia hoc enim (ἐστιν ἀδάρεσον) placitum Domino. Tit. 2: 9. Δούλος ἐν πᾶσιν ἀδαρέσους, servos in omnibus placentes esse, propriis Dominis. Heb. 11: 6. sine fide impossibile esse ἀδαρεσῆσαι, placere Deo. Delectatur enim Deus summopere imagine sua, cuius bona opera sunt effecta.
units.tr: For, (1) Holy Scripture nowhere has a single passage in which the word merit or to merit is found. In Heb. 13:16 the Greek has ἀδάρεσιν [εὐαρεστεῖται], which is more properly rendered "is pleased"; the Vulgate likewise rendered ἀδάρεσον and ἀδαρεσεόμαι [εὐάρεστον, εὐαρεστοῦμαι] as "pleasing" and "to please" in Col. 3:20: "Children, obey your parents in all things, for this is pleasing [ἐστιν εὐάρεστον] to the Lord." Tit. 2:9: "Servants pleasing [εὐαρέστους] their own masters in all things." Heb. 11:6: "Without faith it is impossible to please [εὐαρεστῆσαι] God." For God takes great delight in his own image, whose good works have been produced by him.

units.la: 2. Apud Veteres Patres vox meriti & merendi sensu papistico per multa secula fuit incognita, ut & distinctio meriti in congruum & condignum, quod doctiores ex Pontificiis non latet. Calvinus fatetur huius vocabuli apud veteres usum, sed posteriorum abusum deplorat. Nam veteribus mereri idem erat, quod acquirere, vel etiam habere & obtinere sine dignitate aliqua. Ut cùm Gregorius peccatum vocat felicem culpam, quæ tantum meruit habere redemptorem. Sic passim apud Augustinum, Cyprianum, Fulgentium & alios. 3. Tota Oeconomia redemptionis generis humani per Christum factæ commentum meriti operū ex condigno refutat. In ea duo maxima beneficia sunt spectanda, ius filiationis Dei, Apostolo θεοσέβεια dictum & hoc consequens vita æterna.
units.tr: (2) Among the early Fathers the word merit and to merit in the Papist sense was unknown for many centuries, as was the distinction of merit into congruous and condign, which the more learned among the Papists do not conceal. Calvin admits the use of this word among the ancients but laments the abuse of later writers. For to the ancients "to merit" meant the same as "to acquire", or even "to have and obtain", without any worthiness. Thus when Gregory calls sin a happy fault, which merited to have such a Redeemer. So also everywhere in Augustine, Cyprian, Fulgentius and others. (3) The whole economy of the redemption of mankind wrought by Christ refutes the invention of merit of works in the condign sense. In it two very great benefits are to be considered: the right of sonship of God, which the Apostle calls theosebeia [θεοσέβεια], and eternal life, which follows from this.

units.la: Primum illud summè erat necessarium, quia vita æterna est hæreditas quæ non nisi filiis contingit. Jus hoc acquisivit Christus, Eph. 1: 5. Gal. 4: 5. & nobis applicatur per fidem, Rom. 4: 6. nullo nostro merito sive acquisitionem, sive applicationem spectes. Non respectu illius, quia Christus pro impiis mortuus est, cùm adhuc nullis essemus viribus, Rom. 5: 6. cùm adhuc essemus peccatores, v. 8. cùm Dei inimici essemus, v. 10. & per lapsus mortui, Eph. 2: 5. Nec huius respectu, quia fides est donum Dei ut scriptura docet, Phil. 1: 29. Matth. 16: 17. Ubi ergo meritum hic ex condigno in homine impio, destituto omnibus viribus, peccatore, inimico Dei, & in peccatis mortuo, omni etiam fide carente?
units.tr: The first of these was absolutely necessary, because eternal life is an inheritance, which falls only to sons. Christ acquired this right, Eph. 1:5; Gal. 4:5, and it is applied to us through faith, Rom. 4:6, with no merit of ours, whether you look at its acquisition or its application. Not with regard to any merit, because Christ died for the ungodly, when we were still without strength, Rom. 5:6; when we were still sinners, v. 8; when we were enemies of God, v. 10; and dead through trespasses, Eph. 2:5. Nor with regard to any merit of ours, because faith is the gift of God, as Scripture teaches, Phil. 1:29; Matt. 16:17. Where then is there condign merit in a man who is ungodly, destitute of all strength, a sinner, an enemy of God, dead in sins, and lacking even faith?

units.la: Posterius beneficium, nempe possessio vitæ æternæ, requirit equidem bona opera, & proponitur reconciliatis Deo tanquam merces bonorum operum, interim omne meritum ex condigno excludit. Requirit, inquam, bona opera, propter statum in quem sunt collocati. Sunt enim in statu filiorum Dei, egressi ex statu pristinæ conversationis, & vocati ad sanctimoniam, 1. Thess. 4: 7. Unde necessum est, ut opera sancta præstent 1. propter sanctissimum Deum, cuius facti sunt filii. 1. Pet. 1: 14, 15. Ut filij obedientes, sicut is qui vos vocavit sanctus est ipsi quoque sancti reddamini 2. Propter gratitudinem quam Deo debent,
units.tr: The second benefit, namely the possession of eternal life, indeed requires good works and is set before those reconciled to God as the reward of good works; yet it excludes every condign merit. It requires good works, I say, because of the state into which they have been placed. For they are in the state of the sons of God, having come out of their former manner of life, and called to holiness, 1 Thess. 4:7. Hence it is necessary that they perform holy works: first, on account of the most holy God, whose sons they have become, 1 Pet. 1:14, 15: As obedient children, since he who called you is holy, be holy yourselves also. Second, on account of the gratitude they owe to God,

units.la: 1.Cor.6:20. Empti estis pretio, glorificate igitur Deum in corpore vestro & in spiritu vestro, quae sunt Dei. Huc respexit Christus, Luc. 17: 9. Num gratiam habet Dominus servo, qui fecit quae ipsi praecepta fuerant? Non puto inquit salvator. 3. Quia via sunt & medium per quod ad vitam aeternam pervenitur. Apoc. 22:14,15. Beati qui praestant ejus mandata, ut sit ejus jus in arborem vitae & per portas ingrediantur in civitatem. Foris autem erunt canes, & venefici & scortatores, & homicidae & idololatrae, &c. 4. Propter aedificationem proximi, Matth. 5: 16. Ita splendeat lux vestra coram hominibus, ut videant vestra bona opera, glorificent Patrem vestrum qui est in coelis.
units.tr: 1 Cor. 6:20: You were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God's. Christ had this in mind, Luke 17:9: Does the master thank the servant because he did what was commanded him? I think not, says the Saviour. Third, because they are the way and the means by which eternal life is reached. Rev. 22:14, 15: Blessed are those who keep his commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life and may enter the city by the gates. Outside are the dogs, and the sorcerers, and the fornicators, and the murderers, and the idolaters, etc. Fourth, for the edification of the neighbour, Matt. 5:16: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

units.la: Omne autem meritum ex condigno excludit. Primo, quia vita aeterna est haereditas, haereditas autem non datur propter meritum. Secundo, est haereditas aeterna & infinita, opera autem humana sunt finita, inter quae nulla est proportio, quia infinitum finito est infinitè maius.
units.tr: But every condign merit is excluded. First, because eternal life is an inheritance, and an inheritance is not given on account of merit. Second, it is an eternal and infinite inheritance, whereas human works are finite, and there is no proportion between them, because the infinite is infinitely greater than the finite.

units.la: Quæcunque ergo satisfactiones sint, quæ ieiunia, quæ flagellationes, dicendum cum Apostolo, Rom. 8: 18. Æstimo minimè esse paria, quæ præsenti tempore perpetimur gloriæ in nobis retegendæ. Tertiò Bona opera fidelium nec ipsorum sunt opera, nec perfecta opera, qualia requirit meritum vitæ æternæ. Non prius. Nam sicuti in παραπτώσει Adamus animam & corpus cum omnibus utriusq; facultatibus à Deo accepit, & eius respectu, ut Durandus erudite disputavit, homo ex condigno nihil mereri potuit apud Deum, quia inter creatorem & creaturam nulla potest dari mutua obligatio: ita in παλιγγενεσία non minùs omnia à Deo obtinet fidelis, ut non immeritò Apostolus, eam ipsam ob causam, omnem gloriationem hominibus ademerit, dicendo, si autem accepisti cur gloriaris? Unde sancti sibi conscii huius benignitatis divinæ, nolebant coronas capiti imponere, sed eas proýciebant ante thronum dicentes, tu Domine dignus es qui accipias gloriam, Apoc. 4:10, 11. A' quibus utinam discerent sapere Pharisæi Romanenses.
units.tr: Whatever satisfactions there may be, whatever fasts and scourgings, we must say with the Apostle, Rom. 8:18: I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed in us. Third, the good works of the faithful are neither their own works nor perfect works, such as the merit of eternal life requires. Not the former: for just as in the fall Adam received soul and body with all their faculties from God, and with respect to him, as Durandus learnedly argued, man could merit nothing from God in the condign sense, since no mutual obligation can exist between Creator and creature; so in regeneration the faithful obtains everything from God no less, so that the Apostle not without reason, for this very cause, took away all boasting from men, saying: If you received it, why do you boast? Hence the saints, conscious of this divine kindness, were unwilling to place crowns on their heads, but cast them before the throne, saying: "You, Lord, are worthy to receive glory", Rev. 4:10, 11. Would that the Roman Pharisees would learn wisdom from them!

units.la: Non posterius; quia experientia & scriptura docet sanctificationem propter reliquias pravæ concupiscentiæ & hinc ortæ inter spiritum & carnem luctæ, in hac vita non esse perfectam. Ideo necessum habent sancti ut eorum stolæ dealbentur in sanguine Agni, Apocal. 7:14.
units.tr: Nor the latter; because experience and Scripture teach that sanctification, on account of the remnants of depraved concupiscence and the struggle between spirit and flesh arising from it, is not perfect in this life. Therefore the saints must have their robes washed white in the blood of the Lamb, Rev. 7:14.

units.la: IV. Quod confirmatio, matrimonium, extrema unctio, humana inventa sint non sacramenta ecclesiæ.
units.tr: IV. That confirmation, matrimony, extreme unction and human inventions are not sacraments of the Church.

units.la: Ad hæc unum illud D. Polani replico; ante Hugonem de sancto victore & Petrum Lombardum Magistrum sententiarum nullus Patrum septem sacramenta statuit. Concilium etiam nullum extat antiquius Florentino, in quo numerus septem sacramentorum approbetur. Vixit autem Hugo à Polano citatus, anno post incarnationem Domini 1130. Lombardus vero anno 1140. Confirmatio facta ab Eugenio IV. Papa in Concilio Florentino (& quidem contra scripturam & antiquitatem) anno 1439. Ecce antiquitatem, quam toties obiectant nobis Pontificii.
units.tr: To these things I reply with this one point of Dr. Polanus: Before Hugh of St. Victor and Peter Lombard, the Master of the Sentences, none of the Fathers laid down seven sacraments. Nor does any council exist older than the Council of Florence, in which the number of seven sacraments is approved. Hugh, whom Polanus cites, lived in the year of the Lord's incarnation 1130, and Lombard in 1140. The confirmation of the seven was made by Pope Eugene IV at the Council of Florence (and indeed against Scripture and antiquity) in 1439. Here is the antiquity which the Papists so often throw in our faces.

units.la: Quintum quod hic objcit de continen- tia partim falsum est, partim Luthero ob- jectum.
units.tr: The fifth point that he objects here about continence is partly false, and partly objected to Luther.

units.la: Hæc sunt quæ Harscherus ex Staphylo nobis hactenus obiecit, quibus mendaciis voluit Apostata (nam Lutheranus antea erat Staphylus) suam sinceritatem in religione Papistica ecclesiæ Romanæ obsignare.
units.tr: These are the things that Harscherus has so far objected to us from Staphylus. With these lies the Apostate (for Staphylus was formerly a Lutheran) wished to seal his sincerity in the Papist religion of the Roman Church.

units.la: Testimonia scripturæ impertinenter sunt citata, primò, quia Harscherus præsupponit omnis generis hæreticos facere unum nobiscum regnum, similiter ut olim Pharisæi Christo obiiciebant, ipsum & Beelzebulem conspirare, cuius virtute Dæmonia eiiciat. Quos Christus etiam locis ab Harschero citatis refutat. Deinde non loquitur servator de contentionibus aut rixis minoribus, sed gravioribus, quibus regnū in partes scinditur, nam in græco est μεμερισμένη in partes dissectum, vix enim in hoc mundo ecclesia datur, quæ dissensionibus careat. In ecclesia Christi etiam eo adhuc corporaliter præsente, altercabantur discipuli eius. Matt. 20:24. In ecclesia Corinthiaca dissensiones erant, ut etiam in ecclesia Galatarum.
units.tr: The testimonies of Scripture are cited irrelevantly. First, because Harscherus presupposes that all kinds of heretics make one kingdom with us, just as the Pharisees once charged Christ that he and Beelzebub conspired together, by whose power he cast out demons. Christ refutes these very charges in the passages Harscherus cites. Next, the Saviour is not speaking of minor quarrels or squabbles, but of the graver divisions by which a kingdom is torn into parts; for in the Greek it is divided into parts [μεμερισμένη]. Indeed, in this world a church scarcely exists that is free from dissensions. Even in the Church of Christ, while he was still bodily present, his disciples quarrelled among themselves (Matt. 20:24). There were dissensions in the Corinthian church, as also in the churches of the Galatians.

units.la: Augustini dictum illos attinet, qui putant hominem in quavis religione servari posse, quales sunt Paracelsistæ & horum complices, nos nihil tale statuimus. Illud vero de amicitia Herodis & Pilati est scomma.
units.tr: The saying of Augustine concerns those who think a man can be saved in any religion, such as the Paracelsians and their accomplices; we hold nothing of the kind. But that remark about the friendship of Herod and Pilate is a mere scoff.

units.la: AERIANI SIVE Aerij.
units.tr: AERIANS, OR THE FOLLOWERS OF AERIUS.

units.la: Dicti sunt ab Aerio de quo scribit S. Epiphanius in anacephaleosi 80. haereseon. Presbyter hic erat Episcopi Eustathij, qui pro Ariano habitus est, & ab Episcopatu rejectus. Quandoquidem verò ipse Aerius non constitutus est Episcopus pro Eustathio multa contra ecclesiam docuit, fide quidem existens Arianus perfectissimus, verum amplius docet non oportere offerre pro his qui dormierunt. Sanctus Augustinus tom. 6. de haeresibus haeres. 53. ait Aërium docuisse orare vel offerre pro mortuis oblationem non oportere. S. Damascenus lib. de centum haeresibus, negat, inquit, Aerius quicquam esse pro mortuis offerendum. Unde vides, quâ fide Melanchton in apologia confessionis Augustanae scribat. Falsò etiam citant contra nos damnationem Aerij, quem dicunt propterea damnatum esse, quòd negaverit in Missa oblationem fieri pro vivis & mortuis. Sæpe hoc colore utuntur; allegant veteres haereses & cum his falsò comparant nostram causam, ut illa collatione pragravent nos. Epiphanius testatur, Aerium scripsisse, quòd orationes pro defunctis sint inutiles. Id reprehendit. Neq; nos Aërio patrocinamur &c. Quibus bus verbis duplex falsitas committitur. 1. Aerium tantum negasse orationes pro mortuis, cum etiam de oblationibus loquatur. 2. Quod omnes negantes purgatorium, uti Lutherani sunt, orationes pro mortuis negare debeant, & Aerio patrocinari. Praeterea negabat Aerius non servanda esse statuta jejunia, sed quemlibet jejunare debere cum liberet, ne videretur legi subesse. Asserebat insuper presbyterum ab Episcopo nullo discrimine discerni.
units.tr: They take their name from Aerius, of whom St Epiphanius writes in his summary of the eighty heresies. This man was a presbyter under Bishop Eustathius, who was regarded as an Arian and was removed from the episcopate. Since Aerius was not made bishop in Eustathius's place, he taught many things against the Church. He was an out-and-out Arian in faith, but he further taught that one should not offer for those who have fallen asleep. St Augustine, in his book on heresies (vol. 6, heresy 53), says that Aerius taught that prayer or offering for the dead ought not to be made. St Damascene, in his book on the hundred heresies, says: "Aerius denies that anything should be offered for the dead." From this you can see with what good faith Melanchthon writes in his Apology for the Augsburg Confession. They also falsely cite against us the condemnation of Aerius, whom they say was condemned because he denied that an oblation is made in the Mass for the living and the dead. They often use this pretext: they bring up ancient heresies and falsely compare our cause with them, so as to weigh us down by that comparison. Epiphanius testifies that Aerius wrote that prayers for the departed are useless. He reproves this. Nor do we defend Aerius, etc. In these words a double falsehood is committed. 1. Aerius denied only prayers for the dead, whereas Epiphanius also speaks of oblations. 2. Because all who deny purgatory, as the Lutherans do, must deny prayers for the dead and defend Aerius. Besides, Aerius denied that the fasts prescribed by the Church were to be observed, and said that each person ought to fast when he pleased, so as not to seem subject to the law. He further asserted that a presbyter is not to be distinguished from a bishop by any difference.

units.la: CASTIGATIO.
units.tr: CASTIGATION.

units.la: Aerium haereticum nunc in theatrum producit P. Harscher, de quo ex Epiphanio, Augustino & Damasceno docet 1. Aerium Arianum fuisse, eamq; ob causam ab Episcopatu reiectum.
units.tr: Harscher now brings the heretic Aerius onto the stage. Drawing on Epiphanius, Augustine and Damascene, he teaches: 1. that Aerius was an Arian, and for that reason was removed from the episcopate.

units.la: 2. Habuisse alia quaedam dogmata, utpote primo non oportere offerre pro his qui obdormierunt: secundo non servanda esse statuta ieiunia. Hoc, credo, voluit dicere, quamvis contrarium asserat, cum scribit: Praeterea negabat Aerius non servanda esse statuta jejunia. 3. Presbyterum ab Episcopo nullo discrimine discerni. Sic etiam Bellarminus.
units.tr: 2. That he held certain other doctrines, namely, first, that one should not offer for those who have fallen asleep; second, that the fasts prescribed by the Church are not to be observed. I think he meant this, although he asserts the contrary when he writes: Besides, Aerius denied that the prescribed fasts were to be observed. 3.
